editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The 4710 and 4712 error codes, the explicit-bounds requirement, the `postprocessing` value mapping and the unchanged default of 3 all match the English. In entry 44, "assignment" is rendered as "nilai tugasannya". "Tugasan" means homework or task, not variable assignment, and it clashes with the page's own "nilai yang ditetapkan" (entry 43) and "penetapan pemboleh ubah" (entry 20). In the same entry, "yang milik pemboleh ubah mana" reads awkwardly. Entries 67 and 68 keep "circuit" in English ("tiada circuit dijalankan", "penghalaan circuit"), while the rest of the page consistently uses "litar".

examples.source: map each variable name to its assignment

examples.suggested: memetakan setiap nama pemboleh ubah kepada nilai yang ditetapkan kepadanya
examples.why: 'Tugasan' means a task or homework, not a value assignment. Entries 43 and 20 already use 'nilai yang ditetapkan' and 'penetapan'.

examples.suggested: kedudukan aksara mana dalam bitstring yang menjadi milik pemboleh ubah mana
examples.why: 'yang milik' with no verb is ungrammatical and stiff in Malay.
The rest of the page renders circuit as 'litar' (entries 7, 12, 16, 20). The rewritten changelog entries 67 and 68 switch to English 'circuit', which makes the file inconsistent.

editor_note: Entry 28 is faithful and reads naturally: it keeps both the "minimum dan hampir malar" claim and its reason ("hanya satu pusingan QAOA ... parameter litar optimum yang diperoleh pada CPU"), using the same "pusingan"/"instans" terms as entries 15 and 25 (its lowercase "market split" follows the English source, so it is a defensible choice).

The three rewritten entries (40, 41, 44) keep the meaning: the figures (below 10% at width 9 with 10 qubits, 80–90%, about 15% near width 60, N = 50 with 51 qubits) and the calibration caveat are all intact. The rewrites leave English words where the rest of the page uses Malay. Entries 41 and 44 say "circuit" where every other entry says "litar". Entry 44 says "job" where entry 38 says "kerja". Entry 41 says "kalibrasi backend" where entry 22 says "keadaan penentukuran". In entry 41, "Larian penskalaan wakil" is a stiff calque. Entry 22 already words the same idea as "larian ... yang mewakili".

examples.source: Exact results depend on the backend calibration, circuit, and execution settings.

examples.suggested: Keputusan sebenar bergantung pada penentukuran backend, litar, dan tetapan pelaksanaan.
examples.why: Every other entry in the file says 'litar' for circuit, and entry 22 says 'penentukuran' for calibration. Here the circuit term is left in English and calibration is rendered a different way.

examples.suggested: (51 qubit keseluruhan dalam litar ini), dengan membandingkan pelaksanaan mentah dengan tetapan lalai Orbit dalam satu kerja.

editor_note: Entries 72 and 73 are faithful: "gate CNOT dengan Q sebagai kawalan dan qubitnya sendiri sebagai sasaran, kemudian menerapkan gate Hadamard pada Q" keeps the control and target the right way round and the gates in the right order, and "kumpulkan sebutan di atas mengikut hasil pengukuran pada qubit A dan Q" uses the correct Malay math term "sebutan" for terms, with the math left unchanged.

None of the three rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 78 keeps the degenerate optima, first-solution and variable_mapping details intact, and entry 87 keeps all four recommendations. Entry 53 writes "pemetaan circuit", but every other entry on the page uses "litar" for circuit (entries 52, 64, 67), so it should be "pemetaan litar". Entry 53 also opens with the colloquial "Kalau" where the rest of the page uses the documentation style that calls for "Jika". In entry 87, "Rujuk panduan ... untuk panduan terperinci" repeats "panduan" for both "guide" and "walkthrough", which reads clumsily.

examples.suggested: Jika anda mahu pemetaan litar boleh dihasilkan semula merentas larian

'Kalau' is conversational. The rest of the page uses the standard documentation register, where 'Jika' or 'Sekiranya' is expected.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout, including the fault-tolerant caveat in [37] and the error-mitigation and error-detection definitions in [81] and [90]. The register is uneven. The page switches between "anda" ([0]) and casual "kamu" ([5], [14]), and colloquial "ni/dah/nak/Guna" in [4], [5] and [9] sits next to formal "ini" in [15], [27] and [37]. Eight link titles are still in English ([22], [28], [29], [35], [47], [84], [85], [87]) while their neighbours are translated. "Benchmark" appears as both "Penanda aras" ([46], [86]) and "Tanda aras" ([60]). "Sampler primitif" and "Estimator primitif" ([79], [83]) copy the English word order; Malay would say "primitif Sampler" and "primitif Estimator".

examples.suggested: jika ini kali pertama anda menjalankan kod pada komputer kuantum

Left in English, while sibling titles such as [33] 'Latihan kernel kuantum' are translated. The same applies to [22], [28], [29], [35], [84], [85] and [87].
Copies the English modifier order. In Malay the head noun comes first. [83] 'Estimator primitif' has the same problem.

examples.translation: manipulasi Circuit terkawal dan pemprosesan pasca
examples.why: 'pasca-pemprosesan' is the usual Malay technical form. 'pemprosesan pasca' reads as a literal calque, and [90] uses it too.

editor_note: Entry 12 is faithful and reads naturally. "Randomly distributed between positive and negative values" becomes "diagihkan secara rawak antara nilai positif dan negatif", the triangular-arrangement caveat is kept, and "frustrasi ini berganda secara global, membawa kepada jaringan kekangan yang bercanggah" carries the meaning of "compounded globally ... web of conflicting constraints" correctly.

None of the 23 rewritten entries changes the meaning, so a learner would not be misled. The quantities (15 sizes, 20 bitstrings, 60/300 PUBs, 921,600 shots), the conditions and the caveats all match the English. The rewritten entries split core terms. "circuit" appears as "litar" in [0], [5], [34] and [67] but as untranslated "circuit" in [17], [31], [32], [33], [46] and [49]. "unitary" is "uniter" in most entries but "unitari" in [17]. "job" is "tugasan" in [5], [11] and [67] but "job" in [4], [32], [48], [49] and [51]. Entry [5] also misspells "mempartisiken" and leaves "child" untranslated in "tugasan Runtime Batch child". Entry [17] uses the hybrid "bernoise", where entry [14] earlier on the page uses "bising". Entry [1] translates "Qiskit Function" as "Fungsi Qiskit", which goes against the house rule. Entry [67] points readers to a "Setup" section, but that heading is rendered "Persediaan".

examples.why: The hybrid 'bernoise' and the forms 'unitari'/'circuit' conflict with 'bising', 'uniter' and 'litar', which are used elsewhere in the file.
